Summary: On the Feast of Weeks, the appointed burnt offerings, grain offering, and sin offering are brought as the festival offering.
Commandment: Offer the appointed offerings of the Feast of Weeks.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: On the Feast of Weeks, the appointed burnt offerings, grain offering, and sin offering were brought — a ceremonial law for the harvest feast. Its goal was to mark the day of firstfruits with a full offering, the harvest's thanksgiving joined to atonement. It did not address a particular evil; its work was thanksgiving and worship, not restraint. The offerings said the harvest was received with open hands and a clean conscience, given back to the God who gave it.
